title: Tailscale for KOReader
summary: A VPN plugin that lets e-readers sync over a private network.
paragraphs: Many e-reader sync tools only work on a local network, which is awkward when your books live on a server at home. This Lua plugin adds Tailscale VPN support to KOReader on Kindle, Kobo, and PocketBook ARM devices, so the reader can reach your library from anywhere.

I use it with Syncthing and an iOS shortcut as a small distributed library: send an article or book from a phone and it appears on the reader. It works as an alternative to Calibre and Send to Kindle.

title: SerialPM
summary: A project management app built around a visual timeline, developed as an SF State capstone.
paragraphs: SerialPM was my SFSU senior capstone: a project management app that composed visual timelines around each project's progress, with a focus on being flexible to many organizational, calendar, and agile structures. I led a team of five engineers through the full software development lifecycle, managed the hosting and deployment, synced with each engineer, and managed various staged levels of abstraction and complexity for engineer onboarding to the codebase.
The original backend ran on AWS resources that i've since deprovisioned, but the frontend can be run locally with a mock API to showcase task & organization management, the timeline, and chat.

title: Alzheimer’s screening experiment
summary: A random forest classifier on clinical data, evaluated with recall in mind.
paragraphs: An experiment in R that trains a random forest on clinical data to identify likely Alzheimer’s diagnoses.

In an experimental screening setting, we determined a missed case has a far steeper human cost than the model occasionally suggesting unneeded screenings, and found a recall-optimized model that outperformed our literature review baseline.

title: Auto Child Education
summary: A Europa Universalis V mod that picks each child’s education from their traits.
paragraphs: A mod for Europa Universalis V that removes the tedium of educating every child by hand. It scores each child’s traits and assigns the education that fits their strongest match.
I implemented the scoring model and tuned it against how it behaved in the game. It has about 25,000 Steam Workshop subscribers.
